title: Universal locally closed pullback locus for an invertible module
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a flat [def-weil-flat-morphism], proper [def-weil-proper-morphism] morphism of schemes [def-weil-scheme-over-base] of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. For every morphism $g:T\to S$, form the cartesian square $X_T=X\times_S T$ with projections $p:X_T\to T$ and $q:X_T\to X$. Assume that for every such $g$ the canonical map $\mathcal O_T\to p_*\mathcal O_{X_T}$ is an isomorphism. For a finite locally free module $\mathcal E$ on $X$, there is an immersion $j:Z\to S$ of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] such that a morphism $g:T\to S$ factors through $Z$ if and only if there exists a finite locally free module $\mathcal N$ on $T$ with an isomorphism $q^*\mathcal E\cong p^*\mathcal N$.

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma diagonal-picard-flat-proper, Tag 0BDP

proof.text: The universal pushforward hypothesis gives $H^0(X_s,\mathcal O_{X_s})=\kappa(s)$ for every field-valued fibre, so a nontrivial open-and-closed decomposition of a fibre would give a nontrivial idempotent in this field. Thus every fibre is connected and the locally constant rank of $\mathcal E$ is constant on it. For each $r$, let $V_r\subseteq X$ be the open-and-closed locus where $\mathcal E$ has rank $r$. The image $S_r=f(V_r)$ is open by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open] and closed because $V_r\to S$ is proper and [lem-weil-pbc-proper-closed-image] applies. Connectedness of each fibre makes the $S_r$ disjoint, and their union is $S$ because every fibre is nonempty ($H^0(X_s,\mathcal O_{X_s})=\kappa(s)\neq0$). Restrict to $S_r$ and write the rank as $r$.

The sheaves $\mathcal E$ and $\mathcal E^\vee=\mathcal{H}om(\mathcal E,\mathcal O_X)$ are finite locally free, hence of finite presentation and flat over $S$ because $f$ is flat. By [lem-pc-rf-perfect-base-change], $E=Rf_*\mathcal E$ and $E'=Rf_*\mathcal E^\vee$ are perfect and $Lg^*E\cong Rp_*q^*\mathcal E$, $Lg^*E'\cong Rp_*q^*\mathcal E^\vee$ for every $g:T\to S$; in particular $p_*q^*\mathcal E=H^0(Lg^*E)$ and $p_*q^*\mathcal E^\vee=H^0(Lg^*E')$. Since $Lg^*E$ has no cohomology in negative degrees for every $g$ (in particular for $g=\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)\to S$), a perfect complex with this property has, locally on $S$, tor-amplitude in $[0,b]$ for some $b$ (represent it near $s$ by a complex of finite free modules that is minimal at $s$, as in the Tag 0BDP proof); the construction below is local on $S$ and glues by its universal property. Apply [lem-sc-perfect-h0-locally-closed] with $a=0$ and the rank $r$ to $E$ and to $E'$, obtaining immersions $Z\to S$, $Z'\to S$ of finite presentation, and replace $S$ by $Z\times_SZ'$ (the next step shows that every $g$ admitting an $\mathcal N$ factors through both). On this replacement $f_*\mathcal E$ and $f_*\mathcal E^\vee$ are finite locally free of rank $r$ and their formation commutes with arbitrary base change.

source.place: Tag 0BDP proof, perfect direct-image and locally closed locus paragraphs

proof.text: Let $g:T\to S$. If $q^*\mathcal E\cong p^*\mathcal N$ with $\mathcal N$ finite locally free, then by [lem-pc-projection-formula] and the item's hypothesis $\mathcal O_T\cong p_*\mathcal O_{X_T}$ we get $p_*q^*\mathcal E\cong\mathcal N\otimes p_*\mathcal O_{X_T}\cong\mathcal N$ and likewise $p_*q^*\mathcal E^\vee\cong\mathcal N^\vee$, of rank $r$, and this persists after every further base change $T'\to T$ (the hypothesis holds for $T'\to S$ too); so $g$ factors through $Z\times_SZ'$ and the cup-product pairing $p_*q^*\mathcal E\otimes p_*q^*\mathcal E^\vee\to\mathcal O_T$ is perfect. Conversely, if this pairing between the two rank-$r$ bundles is perfect, choose locally on $T$ bases $\sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_r$ and $\tau_1,\dots,\tau_r$ with $\sigma_i\tau_j=\delta_{ij}$; the maps $(\sigma_i):\mathcal O_{X_T}^{\oplus r}\to q^*\mathcal E$ and $(\tau_j):q^*\mathcal E\to\mathcal O_{X_T}^{\oplus r}$ are inverse, so $q^*\mathcal E\cong p^*p_*q^*\mathcal E$.

Since $f_*\mathcal E$ and $f_*\mathcal E^\vee$ commute with base change, the cup-product pairing over $T$ is the pullback of the pairing $f_*\mathcal E\otimes f_*\mathcal E^\vee\to\mathcal O_S$, and it is perfect exactly over the open locus of $S$ where its determinant (in local bases) is invertible; this open is retrocompact, so its inclusion is of finite presentation. Composing with the immersion of the preceding step and taking the disjoint union over the rank components $S_r$ gives an immersion $j:Z\to S$ of finite presentation, and the preceding equivalence says that $g:T\to S$ factors through $Z$ if and only if $q^*\mathcal E\cong p^*\mathcal N$ for some finite locally free $\mathcal N$ on $T$.
